title: Maple: Ancient Maples You Can Visit
meta_description: Three maples nobody has named to species: a disputed 1895 or 1915 roadside crown in Badhoevedorp, and Utrecht pairs that flower red before their leaves.
intro: These are the maples nobody has narrowed to species, recorded at genus level because the field evidence was never gathered or settled. Badhoevedorp's roadside maple grows in a private front garden, and the register disagrees with itself: one entry bands its planting to 1910-1920, another note says 1895, which would put the tree on the dike before the house beside it was built. Utrecht holds two more, both filed by their neighbours rather than their own names. One stands south of a memorial beech in Zonnenburg, a bastion park Jan David Zocher jr laid out in 1835, sycamore or Norway maple depending on how its winged seeds hang. The other pair, by the Andrea monument in Wilhelminapark, flowers red in February before a single leaf opens, most likely silver maples by their pale, deeply cut foliage, though nobody has confirmed it from a leaf underside yet.
